clue.text: Name that 'Monaco-worth-a-trek' bloke! NB He possibly means he got there!

annotation.answer: THE MAN WHO BROKE THE BANK AT MONTE CARLO

definitions.text: Name that 'Monaco-worth-a-trek' bloke! NB He possibly means he got there!

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the preceding words are only one possible arrangement of their letters, so try another

blocks.note: all thirty-three letters from Name to He are used as fodder

explanation.surface: A quiz challenge to name the gambler who made the trip to Monaco worthwhile by winning big there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and fodder: the music-hall song title, THE MAN WHO BROKE THE BANK AT MONTE CARLO, is rearranged from the letters up to 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous music-hall song celebrates a gambler whose casino winnings at Monaco made his journey there pay handsomely.

clue.text: See 1 across
Off-Broadway location relieves Hamlet production

indicators.note: the phrase is producing, bringing out, a word that sits inside the neighbouring text

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A theatre review: an off-Broadway staging gives some relief to a production of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadway here is not New York but a Cotswold village in Worcestershire, England; EVESHAM is the market town a few miles away.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a town lying just off, that is near, the English village of Broadway in the Vale of Evesham.

clue.text: Blindness of a graduate neurosis: can't see Tyneside

indicators.note: what you can't see is missing, so those letters drop out of the preceding word

blocks.note: taken as written
a Master of Arts is a graduate
taken as written before trimming
Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A medical note on a sufferer's neurosis that leaves them unable to look at Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, the area round Newcastle, lies in the North East of England, the region crosswords abbreviate as NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaurosis is the medical term for partial or total loss of sight without visible damage to the eye.

clue.text: Derek, Clyde and Joe with Louisa May

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women

explanation.surface: A list of first names as if introducing a group of friends joined by the American novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Walcott was the Nobel-winning St Lucian poet, Clyde Walcott a West Indies cricketer and Jersey Joe Walcott a world heavyweight boxing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: All three famous men share the surname, so the plural set of first names points to that family name.

clue.text: Large otter booked with a right turn on the tiles

indicators.note: the letter A beside R for right is turned round, so that pair inside the otter's name flips

blocks.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing label for large
Tarka the Otter is the hero of Henry Williamson's 1927 book

explanation.surface: A big otter from a book goes out for a wild night on the town, taking a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the tiles' looks like the idiom for a night out, but only 'tiles' defines. Ostraka were the shards Athenians voted on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostraka are potsherds, broken pieces of pottery tile on which ancient Athenians scratched names when voting to ostracize.

clue.text: A lover of phonetics

definitions.note: describes the word as belonging to the phonetic alphabet

blocks.note: first meaning: Shakespeare's young lover of Juliet, and so any amorous man
second meaning: the code word for the letter R in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone who simply adores the study of speech sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet runs Alfa, Bravo, Charlie ... Quebec, ROMEO, Sierra; it is a word of phonetics in that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo names a passionate suitor after Shakespeare's hero, and is also the spelling-alphabet code word for R.

clue.text: Fertilizer the shrew absorbs in one

indicators.note: something that absorbs takes material into itself, so the outer name swallows the rest

blocks.note: Kate is the shrew in The Taming of the Shrew
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: a fertilizer that the shrew soaks up all in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: The shrew sounds like the small animal; she is Shakespeare's Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: Kainite is a natural potassium and magnesium salt mineral spread on fields as a potash fertilizer.

clue.text: Wily bobby's sole error: admission of youthful indulgence?

indicators.note: an error puts things wrong, so these letters are set down in the wrong order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A crafty policeman's one mistake was to let some young tearaways off lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying excuses mischief by young men as natural, an admission that their behaviour is indulged.

clue.text: Mix it with whisky, soda and ice, as they say in the East End

indicators.text: as they say in the East End
indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop the H, so the drink's name is heard as they would pronounce it

blocks.note: a highball is whisky and soda with ice in a tall glass; drop the H in Cockney style

explanation.surface: A barman's recipe for mixing a long whisky drink, in London slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix it' looks like a cocktail instruction, but here it is the slang for squaring up to someone. The East End is the Cockney district of London, where H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare them down aggressively, which is squaring up for a fight, or mixing it.

clue.text: One firm push in advance on Mexican port

indicators.note: being in advance means going in front, so this word leads the others

blocks.note: to tamp is to push down firmly
the Roman numeral
short for company

explanation.surface: A single company makes a determined push forward against a Mexican harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm push' reads as one phrase, but firm is the company and push stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampico is a seaport city on the Gulf of Mexico coast in the state of Tamaulipas.

clue.text: Shrink from seaman with utter strumpet

indicators.note: to utter is to speak, so the word that follows is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an able-bodied seaman
a strumpet is a prostitute; said aloud the word is just these sounds

explanation.surface: Recoiling from a sailor who is out with a complete tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it, to recoil or shrink away from it in disgust.

clue.text: Thus I list Rodin's silent retrospective of noted works

indicators.note: to make something silent is to take away its noise, so a word for a racket comes out
looking back, so the whole string is read from end to start

blocks.note: thus means so
taken as written
a rota is a list of duties
the sculptor's name, before its noise is removed

explanation.surface: An art critic introducing a retrospective exhibition of the sculptor Rodin's quiet works.
explanation.walkthrough: Silent Rodin loses its DIN, or noise, leaving RO; SO + I + ROTA + RO reads back as ORATORIOS. Noted works are works set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorios are large-scale musical compositions for voices and orchestra, so they are works written in notes.

clue.text: The other guide to India

blocks.note: surface reading: an alternative travel guidebook for a trip to the subcontinent
setter's reading: 'the other' is British slang for sex, so this is a sex manual from India

explanation.walkthrough: 'The other', as in 'a bit of the other', is British slang for sex; the ancient Sanskrit text is India's famous guide to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Sanskrit treatise on love and sexual technique is India's best-known manual of erotic practice.

clue.text: Offensive Italian-English mountain man?

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
the abominable snowman of the Himalayas; the question mark admits it is a loose description

explanation.surface: A rude Anglo-Italian mountaineer, or an abominable snowman with bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: EYETI, like Eyetie, is an old derogatory British slang word for an Italian, from a mock pronunciation of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dated, insulting British slang term used for a person from Italy.

clue.text: European sinecure falling to rapacity ...

indicators.note: something falling tumbles and lands in disarray, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
an undemanding paid post, used as fodder

explanation.surface: A cushy Brussels job going to someone simply out of greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurience is hunger or greediness, a ravenous craving that matches rapacity, the urge to grab.

clue.text: Meditation here from Massenet: ie wasting time once!

indicators.note: wasting means losing something, so a letter is lost from the phrase

blocks.note: ie stands for id est, that is
T for time, removed once only though the phrase has two

explanation.surface: A music note on Massenet's famous Meditation and how it wasted time long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT IS has two Ts; 'once' says only one goes, the second, giving THAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Massenet's opera Thaïs contains the celebrated violin interlude known as the Méditation, so that piece comes from it.

clue.text: ... with a piece of the Indian islands

blocks.note: with means and, plus
taken as written
a piece in chess or draughts is a man

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: greed coupled with grabbing a share of some islands in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the surface to 14 down, but the wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andaman Islands are an archipelago in the Bay of Bengal belonging to India.

clue.text: Some measure of radioactivity where Montcalm failed to change halves on line

indicators.note: changing the halves swaps the front and back of the place name so each sits in the other's position

blocks.note: General Montcalm lost the city of Quebec to Wolfe in 1759; its two halves are swapped
re means on, concerning
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A historical note: radioactivity measured at the place a French general lost a battle, after swapping halves.
explanation.walkthrough: Montcalm was the French general killed defending Quebec against Wolfe in 1759. The printed grid has BOCQUEREL, a misprint for BECQUEREL.
explanation.definitionFit: The becquerel is the SI unit of radioactivity, one atomic decay per second, named after Henri Becquerel.

clue.text: Manual indicating 'Show yellow card for obstruction'

blocks.note: a referee who shows a yellow card books the player
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A referee's handbook telling them to caution a player for blocking an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' sits naturally in the football surface but is part of the fragment for the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A booklet is a small handbook or instruction manual of a few pages.

clue.text: What it takes to make a bore

blocks.note: first meaning: the quality or ability needed, as in a person of the right sort
second meaning: the internal diameter of a gun barrel

explanation.surface: A wry question about what qualities a tedious person needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the inside width of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means both personal quality or ability and the measured diameter of a gun barrel.

clue.text: Greek pines for this drink

blocks.note: surface reading: a homesick Greek longs for a drink
setter's reading: pine trees supply the resin that flavours this Greek wine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' reads as a verb, longing for, but it is the plural of pine tree, the source of resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a white or rosé Greek wine flavoured with resin from Aleppo pine trees.

clue.text: Some tie and diehard

definitions.note: names the kind of tie the answer precedes

blocks.note: first meaning: the phrase is a kind of tie, the striped neckwear of a former pupil
second meaning: conservative, traditional in outlook

explanation.walkthrough: The old school tie is the striped tie of a British public school, and stands for the network of privilege it marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone old school is traditional and resistant to change, much like a stubborn conservative diehard.

clue.text: See 1 across
Fibre of dark lady eluding ref's assistant

indicators.note: what is eluding escapes and is not caught, so it goes missing from the word

blocks.note: the initials linked to Shakespeare's sonnets, whose 'Mr W.H.' dedication belongs with the Dark Lady poems
a referee's whistle helps control the game

explanation.surface: A sly woman giving a football linesman the slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ref's assistant' suggests a linesman, but it is the referee's whistle; take away WH, from the sonnets' Mr W.H., to leave ISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca leaves, used for cord, brushes and matting.

clue.text: Carton sent for dispatch by this carrier

definitions.text: Carton sent for dispatch by this carrier

blocks.clueFragment: Carton sent for dispatch by this carrier
blocks.note: surface reading: a cardboard box posted with a delivery firm
setter's reading: Sydney Carton of A Tale of Two Cities, carried to the guillotine to be executed

explanation.walkthrough: Carton looks like a box and dispatch like posting, but Sydney Carton goes to his death in Dickens's novel, and dispatch means killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbril was the open cart that carried condemned prisoners to the guillotine during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Great circle round last city in Australia

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the first word wraps the last one

blocks.note: great means big
the last part is the end
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A great circular route round the last city of a trip in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great circle' reads as the navigation term, but the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Bendigo is a former gold-rush city in the state of Victoria, Australia.

clue.text: Either Doris or Robin, eventually

definitions.note: describes either person as a member of the Day family name

blocks.note: first meaning: Doris Day the singer and Sir Robin Day the British television interviewer each share the surname
second meaning: at some unspecified future time

explanation.walkthrough: Doris Day was an American film star and Sir Robin Day a famous British political TV interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at some point in the future, sooner or later, which is what eventually means.
